children: Virgin Galactic inked a deal with the Air Force Research Laboratory's Space Warfare Directorate, under which the company's next-generation spaceship will be evaluated as a platform for capturing space weather data.

Under the 24-month agreement, researchers at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico will evaluate the integration of sensor systems with Virgin Galactic's next-generation Spaceship to collect space weather data during flight, the company said Wednesday.
The collaboration aims to accelerate the understanding of the effect of space weather on space-based infrastructure.

"Understanding space weather dynamics in the mesosphere and lower thermosphere depends on consistent, high-quality observational data, which has remained limited at scale," said Shaun Ard, a senior research chemist at Air Force Research Laboratory.
"This collaboration gives our researchers access to a platform particularly well-suited to fill that gap."
The agreement comes after Virgin Galactic signed a similar cooperative research and development agreement with Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory late last year.
